{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|gbrain setup hermes        # a release binary: ~/.local/bin/gbrain setup hermes
16|```
17|
18|Setup registers gbrain through Hermes's own CLI: it runs `hermes mcp add`
19|(answering its prompts), reads the entry back from `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and
20|checks it with `hermes mcp test gbrain`. Hermes's file tools refuse an agent's edit
21|of `config.yaml` ("Agent cannot modify security-sensitive configuration"), so
22|an agent should run setup rather than edit the file. Setup finds `hermes` on PATH
23|or where Hermes's installer puts it (`~/.local/bin/hermes`,
24|`$HERMES_HOME/hermes-agent/venv/bin/hermes`); with neither it prints the command
25|below. An `mcp_servers.gbrain` entry setup did not write (a hosted URL, say) is
26|left alone, `--dry-run` previews and `--remove` runs `hermes mcp remove gbrain`.
27|A rerun updates gbrain's own entry and keeps its member binding
28|(`--stdio-member`), its connect timeout and, when `GBRAIN_HOME` is unset, the
29|brain it already points at. An entry of gbrain's that carries other settings, or
30|environment variables beyond `GBRAIN_HOME`, is left alone too (setup says which;
31|no stored value goes on a command line). If an update fails, setup puts the
32|previous entry back with `hermes config set` and exits 1.
33|Hermes rewrites `config.yaml` as plain YAML, dropping comments, so setup sets its
34|marked hook block aside around the call and puts it back. Then start a new session.
35|
36|### Register by hand
37|
38|```bash
39|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
40|```
41|
42|With a release binary, put `~/.local/bin/gbrain` in place of `$(which gbrain)`.
43|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
44|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
45|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
46|operation.
47|
48|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
49|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
50|
51|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
52|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
53|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
54|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
55|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
56|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
57|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
58|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
59|  all tools enabled.
60|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
61|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
62|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
63|
64|## Brain-first instructions
65|
66|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
67|brain nobody told them about, so `gbrain setup hermes` also adds the brain-first

69|

74|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
75|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
76|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never

import json, subprocess, sys, os
CMD = ["/harness-state/.gbrain/hook-launcher/gbrain-hook", "/harness-state/.bun/bin/gbrain",
       "serve", "--surface", "starter", "--advertise", "verbs"]
env = dict(os.environ, GBRAIN_HOME="/harness-state")

def session(calls):
    p = subprocess.Popen(CMD, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, env=env, text=True)
    def send(m): p.stdin.write(json.dumps(m) + "\n"); p.stdin.flush()
    def read(i):
        while True:
            line = p.stdout.readline()
            if not line: raise SystemExit("server closed")
            m = json.loads(line)
            if m.get("id") == i: return m
    send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":0,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"rt","version":"1"}}})
    read(0); send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"notifications/initialized"})
    out = []
    for n,(name,args) in enumerate(calls, 1):
        send({"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":n,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":name,"arguments":args}})
        r = read(n)
        txt = "".join(c.get("text","") for c in r.get("result",{}).get("content",[])) or json.dumps(r.get("error"))
        out.append((name, txt))
    p.stdin.close(); p.wait(timeout=30)
    return out

mode = sys.argv[1]
if mode == "remember":
    calls = [("remember", {"fact":"gbrain MCP round-trip marker QX-5150","entity":"gbrain install check",
                          "provenance":"install-check","content_origin":"inferred"})]
elif mode == "recall":
    calls = [("recall", {"entity":"gbrain install check"})]
else:
    calls = [("forget", {"fact_id":int(i), "reason":"install check cleanup"}) for i in sys.argv[2:]]
for name, txt in session(calls):
    print(f"== {name} (pid-separate session)\n{txt[:1500]}\n")

GBrain v0.60.757.0 is installed and connected to this Hermes agent as a keyless local brain. Your identity text is unchanged. Remember and recall both worked over real GBrain calls, but I couldn't confirm recall from a fresh chat session.

Search-mode choice. Install set the mode to conservative because there's no chat key and no reranker. The cost estimates below are the matrix from this release's install output. The install guide's own copy shows older, higher prices.

    Estimated downstream input cost of the retrieved payload @ 10K queries/mo:

                       Haiku 5.5     Sonnet 5.5    Opus 5.5
                       ($0.10/M in)  ($2/M in)     ($4/M in)
       conservative    $4/mo         $80/mo        $160/mo
       balanced        $10/mo        $200/mo       $400/mo
       tokenmax        $20/mo        $400/mo       $800/mo

       Assumed payload: conservative 4K, balanced 10K, tokenmax 20K tokens.
       Scales linearly: x10 for 100K/mo, /10 for 1K.

  1) conservative (in effect): 4K token budget, at most 10 chunks.
  2) balanced: 12K budget, 25 chunks. Its reranker needs a key, so it can't run yet.
  3) tokenmax: no budget, 50 chunks.

Since the brain is keyless, `gbrain search` and recall never expand queries and nothing goes to a cloud provider. To change the mode: `gbrain config set search.mode <mode>`, then check with `gbrain search modes`.

Other first-run settings, defaults in effect:
- Auto-saving facts is off: it saves only what you ask. "salient" is the recommended option (`gbrain config set memory.auto_writeback salient`).
- Free upkeep is on.
- The conversation archive is on; turn it off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`.
- No services, cron jobs or paid providers were set up.

Install:
- The security scanner blocked the documented `curl | bash` and `bun install -g` commands. I installed Bun 1.4.5 from its GitHub release zip instead.
- I used the guide's fallback path: cloned gbrain to `~/gbrain`, checked out commit 915e3b30, then ran `bun install` and `bun link`. That commit is the v0.60.757.0 tag, which is also `latest-stable`.
- `gbrain --version` prints 0.60.757.0. Database setup steps are complete, and the brain is at `~/.gbrain/brain.pglite`.

Hermes changes (`gbrain setup hermes`):
- **SOUL.md:** your identity text is unchanged; a marked "check GBrain first" block was appended after it.
- **config.yaml:** the `gbrain` MCP server was added, plus a marked per-turn reminder hook. `hermes hooks doctor` reports it healthy.
- **Undo:** `gbrain setup hermes --remove`. Backups of the original files are in `/harness-state/hermes/cache/scratch/hermes-pre-gbrain/`.

Verification:
- `hermes mcp test gbrain`: connected, 8 tools found.
- `gbrain doctor --only harness_wiring`: ok.
- Command line: saved a fact containing the code HX-7731, then read it back in a separate process (fact 1). An exact keyword search for a test page also found it.
- MCP, using the same server command Hermes launches: one session saved fact 2 (code QX-5150). A separate session read it back, and so did the command line.
- I couldn't confirm recall from a fresh Hermes chat session. My attempt (`hermes -z`) timed out after about 280s with no output. To check yourself, restart Hermes and ask it to recall the facts for "install-check/note".

Two things to know about the agent's memory tools:
- Facts saved by the agent must name an existing page with its folder (e.g. `install-check/note`). A plain name is refused if no page has it.
- The memory tools Hermes uses don't accept the field that marks where a fact came from (`content_origin`); saves work without it.
